core.text: The one thing that must hold for the main clause to be true is stated by **dummodo + subjunctive (the 'provided that / as long as' condition)**: *Quidquid vīs, estō — dummodo nīl recitēs!* — be whatever you like, provided you recite nothing. The verb is the subjunctive (the form Latin uses for wishes, purposes and what someone tells someone to do): present after a present main verb, imperfect after a past one; the negative is *dummodo nē*. *Modo* and *dum* alone can do the same job: *ōderint, dum metuant* — let them hate, as long as they fear. Latin name: *dummodo cum coniūnctīvō*.
English: *provided that*, *as long as*, *so long as*, *only if*: you can go out, *as long as you're back by ten*. A condition with a warning finger raised.
dummodo / modo / dum + subjunctive = provided that; negative dummodo nē.

invented.en: I will wait, as long as you do not come late.

core.text: *sī* + subjunctive imagines something untrue; *dummodo* + subjunctive lays down a real requirement. *Sī tacērēs, manērem* (if you were quiet — you aren't); *manēbō, dummodo taceās* (I'll stay, as long as you keep quiet — and you can).

more.text: Also easy to confuse: *dum* + the present indicative (the plain statement form) is 'while' in a story — *dum gubernātor loquitur* — while the helmsman is speaking, another ship appears (Week 7); *dum / dummodo* + subjunctive is 'provided that'. The verb form tells you which *dum* you have.

The learner's notes have no page on *dummodo*; the three sentences in the texts are all in Weeks 13–14 (Cornelius on the games, Fabia on Sextus's fighting, Martial's *Quidquid vīs, estō*). Allen & Greenough treat it under clauses of proviso: *dum*, *modo*, *dummodo*, and *tantum ut* take the subjunctive, with *nē* as the negative, and often carry a wish along with the condition — *modo nē lūdat* (only let him not play about).

Related uses of *dum* with the subjunctive: 'until' when there is waiting or intention (*exspectā dum veniat* — wait until he comes), and 'while' + subjunctive for background in some writers. With the indicative *dum* is plain 'while' or 'as long as' (*dōnec ego vīvam*, Week 11, is the same idea with *dōnec*).
